findings.description: Critical: check_test_contract.py ignores deleted test files because +++ /dev/null is skipped without retaining the old test path, so removed assert lines can pass the assertion contract check.
findings.resolution: Track the path from the preceding --- line and scan removed assertion lines when the new path is /dev/null; add a deletion regression test.

findings.description: Critical: verify_behavior_preservation.py resolves --head but runs the HEAD test command in the live repository, so dirty working-tree files or a non-HEAD --head ref can be reported as the resolved head_sha without actually testing that tree.
findings.resolution: Run both baseline and head refs in detached temporary worktrees, or refuse dirty trees and verify the checked-out commit matches head_sha before running tests.

findings.description: Critical: --skip-baseline-run can emit exit 0 and both_passed=true with baseline_run=null, which does not mechanically prove the required dual-run baseline plus HEAD verification.
findings.resolution: Require an explicit prior baseline report or mark both_passed false/unknown when baseline execution is skipped.

findings.description: Critical: assertion detection only matches changed lines that start with assert/expect tokens, so multiline expectation body edits such as changed object fields inside expect(...).toEqual({...}) are missed.
findings.resolution: Track assertion/expect blocks across hunks or parse common test syntaxes enough to flag changed lines inside assertion bodies; add multiline expect/assert regression tests.

findings.description: FYI: verify_behavior_preservation.py executes --test-cmd with shell=True. That is acceptable for trusted operator commands, but becomes shell injection if future callers source the command from repo metadata or untrusted workflow input.
findings.resolution: Document the trust boundary clearly and consider an argv-list mode for non-shell execution.

findings.description: Nit: the check_test_contract.py docstring says characterization commits that add tests are fine, but the implementation and tests intentionally flag pure +assert additions when they are inside the checked range.
findings.resolution: Clarify that --base must point after characterization commits and that any added/removed assertion line in the simplify range fails.

findings.description: none: The main simplify skill text covers the coverage gate, characterization-first workflow, expanded isomorphic/dead-code/redundant-intermediate catalog, manual invocation, and ecosystem routing without auto-wiring simplify into implement or autopilot.
findings.resolution: Keep this structure; it matches the OpenSpec intent and keeps the behavior-preservation contract visible at invocation time.
